decision.reason: The generated contract contains contradictions that can drive a conforming developer toward incorrect behavior.

deductions.finding: nil-removes-field supplies extra although the schema only declares debug, then requires successful deletion and preservation of extra; the task requires ErrUnknownField.
Scenarios require int input 80 to become float64(80), while the task only defines accepted numeric Go types and the spec's own J7 says a single number type is not forced.

The spec and req place the Go module under task-01-configresolver while the task contract defines the submitted module root as the package root; the downstream checklist propagates the same location decision.
Recursive object behavior is demonstrated only with server.host and server.port; no three-level object case closes the hidden recursion boundary.
Determinism compares repeated calls over the same maps and omits logically equal maps constructed in different insertion orders.
The ownership checks cover one nested object but do not explicitly close schema mutation, nested arrays, or all mutable aliases between Result and inputs.
Data == nil is covered, while nil/empty schema and nil/empty sources outcomes remain unspecified.

positive_findings: The document keeps one spec.md and uses direct GIVEN/WHEN/THEN scenarios.
Required deletion and missing behavior use errors.Is with ErrRequiredRemoved.
Race, performance, go test, go vet, and E2E omission are explicitly modeled.
x-req3 preserves Scenario names and propagates the spec contract into an executable checklist.
